themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints skyrocketed to 9 THIS WEEK—a 7,100% spike versus 0.1 average weekly complaints over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 26.84), suggesting a sudden, acute disruption at one or more district parks that warrants urgent investigation into source and timing.
evidence: 9 noise-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 26.84 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Coincides with spike in unleashed dog complaints (5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 avg) and park rules violations (3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 avg), suggesting possible event or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Visit parks at peak hours to document noise sources; interview residents about when/where complaints concentrated
Check if a specific park event, construction, or dog park policy change triggered the surge

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs & Park Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK—a 1,233% spike from 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 9.55)—alongside 3 park rules violations THIS WEEK (1,100% spike), indicating a possible enforcement vacuum or behavioral shift in district parks.
evidence: 5 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 9.55)
3 park rules violations THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35)
Spike clusters with noise-park spike, suggesting concentrated park access or safety issue
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept. about enforcement presence; check if dog run hours or rules changed recently
Talk to residents about specific parks where off-leash dogs are congregating and safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Concern
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints reached 3 LAST WEEK—a 300% spike from 0.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.2)—warranting Health Dept. investigation into potential foodborne illness cluster in the district.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.2 indicates statistically significant spike
311 data alone cannot identify common source—requires Health Dept. follow-up
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH to learn if a specific restaurant, food vendor, or food source is under investigation
Interview affected residents about establishments visited; check for social media reports

themes_detail.label: Pigeon Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary pigeon condition complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK—a 1,100% spike from 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.16)—pointing to a localized pest management problem or feeding activity.
evidence: 3 unsanitary pigeon complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Complements long-running sanitation concerns reflected in budget requests for sewer inspection
reporting_angles: Identify locations of complaints; determine if a specific food source, construction site, or dumping area is attracting pigeons
Interview Sanitation Dept. about pest management response and community outreach

themes_detail.label: Safety Complaints Elevated
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints reached 10 THREE WEEKS AGO—a 248% spike from 2.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.62)—though this is not THIS WEEK's data, it represents a recent sustained concern warranting follow-up on whether conditions have improved or persisted.
evidence: 10 safety complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
No follow-up data THIS WEEK; unclear if spike was transient or ongoing
reporting_angles: Check if safety complaints have continued at elevated levels or returned to baseline
Interview NYPD and community board about incidents from 3 weeks ago; determine nature of safety concerns (street violence, vehicle collisions, etc.)
